page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-48GB is a virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor within the Cloud Native family. It is equipped with 8 shared vCPUs mapped to AMD EPYC 7542 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include standard AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions, alongside 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1d cache. Memory capacity is configured at 48.0 GB of RAM, offering a ratio of 6.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local storage, dedicated hardware GPUs, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage.

Benchmark measurements indicate reliable general-purpose compute metrics coupled with specific memory throughput characteristics. The instance achieved 10082.0 points in Geekbench multi-core testing and a strong single-core score of 1996.0 points, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 15622.7. In multi-threaded compression tasks, bzip3 reached 75.93 GB/sec, while static web serving registered 6.72 GB/sec. Conversely, raw synthetic stress-ng single-core compute performance placed in the lower 10% with 783.78 points, and multi-core stress-ng reached 6258.8. Memory read bandwidth measured 830.42 GB/sec for small cached blocks, but drops to 36.84 GB/sec read and 17.27 GB/sec write for large 256 MB uncached buffers.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances 8 shared physical cores against an above-average memory allocation of 48.0 GB. This resource density makes it cost-efficient for memory-sensitive enterprise software stacks without the expense of dedicated-core configurations. Tradeoffs center on the shared CPU allocation, which can cause variability during peak sustained computation, and the modest uncached memory bandwidth, which constrains large-model AI inference as shown by the 6.18 tokens/sec rate on 7B LLM text generation.

Given its high RAM-to-core ratio and solid middle-tier database operations score of 4722.5 alongside 12.3 million Redis SET operations per second, UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-48GB is well suited for in-memory caching layers, medium relational databases, containerized backend services, ETL preprocessing pipelines, and web application hosting.

Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance does not include integrated local disk storage or dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance firmly in the mid-range across core enterprise metrics, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 10082.0, a PassMark CPU score of 15622.7, and 12.3 million Redis SET operations per second. While small cached reads achieve high bandwidth, uncached memory writes (17.27 GB/sec) and sustained single-core stress tests reflect standard shared-core constraints. Offering cost-effective RAM density, this server profile is best suited for memory-intensive caching systems, relational database workloads, container fleets, and multi-threaded web serving.
